newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rally at close on S&P news.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rally at close on S&P news.

text.p: Argentine stocks bucked the trend on Wall Street and rallied at the close Wednesday on the back of a sovereign debt upgrade by Standard & Poor's, dealers said.

"The market was clearly favored by the upgrade which took us by surprise today and allowed the bolsa to pry itself apart from the international context, with another dismal session for the Dow," said Emilio Alessandro at brokers Alessandro.
The blue-chip MerVal index erased slim early losses around midsession, immediately after the S&P upgrade, and closed up 1.9 percent at 729.01.
This contrasted with a loss of 1.4 percent for the Dow.
The MerVal still stands 1.4 percent lower on the week after diving 4.5 percent Monday.

"The bolsa outperformed all of the Latin American markets today but we shouldn't be overly enthusiastic, because volume remains very thin and the big players aren't taking any chances," said an analyst at a large local brokerage.
Floor volume was paltry at 16.8 million pesos against 17 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter turnover shrank to a token 59.3 million pesos.
"People are still waiting for key U.S. economic indicators Friday, and the performance of the markets in the next 48 hours will be crucial to see if this recovery can last," Alessandro said.
He said signs Argentina and Brazil were overcoming a trade row would also underpin the bolsa.
The broad market index closed up 1.0 percent, with winners bashing losers 37 to 11 and 15 issues closing flat.
Top MerVal risers were carmaker Ciadea, which surged 6.7 percent, oil firm Astra, up 4.0 percent, and electricity firm Central Costanera and steelmaker Siderar, both up 3.2 percent.
The only main-tier loser was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, off 3.0 percent.
Pepsi bottler Baesa, a second-line stock, fell 4.3 percent on news it failed to meet $500 million in debt payments due March 31.
